As Jews around the world go into this holiday, we look to atone for our sins.
Thanks for reading Michael's Substack! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.
[Pledge your support](https://substack..3HVAbsWS3ratdDIIc2hq-DIFpe_9Ax1JnYWsc84OpbY?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=150100293)
_I am not perfect and no one is; this time of 25 hours of reflection is to look where we have been wrong and where we can do better._
_**I entered this political race as a calling and every day we are working hard to do better to win this November to Take Back Connecticut and Heal this Country.**_
I cannot call out all of the sins of my opponent (as there are too many) but there are a few glaring ones that come to mind this year:
1. **Voting against the Israel Security Assistance Support Act**

* This bill specified that no federal funds may be used to withhold, halt, reverse, or cancel the delivery of defense articles or defense services to Israel.
* As someone who claims to be a friend of Israel, Jim failed to stand up to defend Israel
* After October 7th, Jim posted a message supporting the Council of American Islamic Relations (CAIR) and claims to support Israel
* Jim cannot support both Israel and CAIR and take funds from AIPAC

2. **Voting against the "Violence Against Women by Illegal Aliens Act".**

* This is a bill that expands the crimes and other grounds for which illegals are deportable.
* This amendment makes any sex offense (including crimes against minors) or conspiracy to commit a sex offense a basis for deportation.
* The bill also expands the domestic violence crimes to deport illegals that engage in physical or sexual abuse or a pattern of coercive behavior when it occurs within certain close relationships.

_**This bill should have no opposition and to allow such behavior by those illegals who broke laws to enter this country to take it further to commit violent acts against women and children and violate additional criminal laws is truly a sin to allow.**_
3. **Voting against the "Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act or the SAVE Act"**

* This bill is critical to voter integrity as it requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship in order to register to vote in federal elections.
* This bill requires states to remove non-citizens from their voter roles.
* This bill also allows legal action against election officials that fail in their duties to register applicants and provide criminal penalties for certain offenses.

_**Election integrity is critical and voter ID is critical to fair elections. it is tragic that it has gone along partisan lines. We know someone who can vote with his supermarket card even though he has proper federal identification.**_
We are here fighting a David v. Goliath battle as the underdog. We could use your support so we can get the message out and volunteers to help spread the word.
[Donate](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/4d3a6d6f-acbe-499e-b226-be3b9a358511?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I ask for two things from you -
1. Support where you can; and
2. Send our content to friends to expand the base

Have an easy fast for those fasting and a sweet new year for us all when you take action at the ballot box this November.
Sharing is Caring - so if you like the message please pass it on.
Thank you for your continued support. We could really use it to get the message out to many others.

Peter, An explosive new investigative report from Drop Site News alleges that U.S. Secretary of State Anthony Blinken gave the green light to Netanyahu to withhold humanitarian aid from Gaza just days after October 7, 2023 by signing off on a policy to “thwart” aid that Israel claimed was being commandeered by Hamas.

It’s also a matter of record that over 280 humanitarian aid workers were subjected to Israel’s preferred manner of “thwarting” aid by way of assassinating the heroic workers attempting to get that life-saving aid to the people of Gaza.

When asked about the allegations that Blinken signed off on a policy that would deny life-saving aid to Gaza, State Department spokesperson Matthew Miller called it “absurd”, but then went on to all but confirm those allegations by admitting that there’s been very few cases of aid trucks being commandeered by Hamas. Meanwhile, hundreds of humanitarian aid workers have been targeted for assassination by Israel. As children starve to death, the Biden-Harris administration has stayed the deadly course by funding Israel’s genocidal war crimes while declaring their unwavering support for the Netanyahu regime.[**

For so long, folks around here said we couldn't win. Maybe they were used to accepting more of the same, or maybe they simply couldn't imagine the impossible.

**Until our movement made the impossible, possible.**

Thousands of supporters have joined our movement from all over the country, helping us build a formidable movement.

Now, our campaign has been in all 82 counties knocking on doors and listening to every voter we come across.

But, we need your help to keep our voter outreach going strong. # Hello Peter!
---
| Believe it or not, there are only 5 days left before people start voting and the last day to register to vote is next Tuesday, October 15th! We have to do all we can over the next 24 days to keep my seat blue, ensure that Vice President Harris defeats Donald Trump, and elect Democrats up and down the ballot.
This weekend, I’ll be hitting the campaign trail and joining local Democrats running for office in Springfield, Corvallis, and Eugene. The following weekend, I will be joining volunteers as we knock on doors and engage with voters in Port Orford and Coos Bay! To get involved and hear from local candidates helping to kick off our canvassing events, RSVP below.
Today, I’m taking to the debate stage with my opponents at the Eugene City Club’s Candidate Forum. There I will be detailing my plan to continue to protect working families, build more housing and ensure a fair economy as your Congresswoman.
Help us fill the room to show that we stand for democracy!
Keep reading to see how you can help make a change as we work together to build a country that works for all of us.
---
|
---
|
# Volunteer Opportunities
We have several exciting volunteer opportunities coming up, and we would love for you to be a part of them. Whether you have a few hours to spare or can commit to helping on a weekly basis, your help is invaluable to us!
**Canvasses** Help engage voters for the 2024 election through direct conversations about what is at stake this election. This is a great way to engage with your local community and spread our campiagn’s message.

| **Message from the Congresswoman**
---
|
With 24 days until the election, I can’t emphasize enough how important these next few weeks will be.
In the past 3 months, our team of volunteers has knocked on over 15,000 doors and engaged thousands of voters in meaningful conversations about what’s at stake in this election. But the work is not over. Everything we have been working towards comes down to this next month.
As Americans, it is our duty to play an active role in shaping our democracy. Whether that means volunteering to knock on doors, donating or talking with your friends and family, every ounce of effort we put in matters!
Thank you for joining me in this fight so I can continue fighting to represent Oregon in Congress.
Together we can keep my seat blue, elect Hakeem Jeffries as the Speaker of the House and elect Kamala Harris as our next President.
Sincerely,

Hey everybody, ⚠️ **Tuesday** **is an important deadline** : it’s the last day to register in advance to vote on Election Day! Registering in advance will save you time if you’re planning to vote in person on Tuesday, November 5. **The deadline to register in advance is 11:59pm this Tuesday, October 15.** [Check your registration status](https://votereedolson.us/l/9YjpgInFtEGD) and make sure you’re good to go.
---
[ Am I Registered to Vote? ](https://votereedolson.us/l/CsmjRHh5iebD)
---
If you’re already registered to vote, don’t forget [you can vote early right now](https://votereedolson.us/l/a4HN4V9IktUw)! See the info below on how to vote early. **We need everyone to get out the vote to get us to victory this year!**
---
|
---
**🗳️ Early In Person**
---
All voters have the option to vote early in person. To cast your ballot in person, go to the following locations:
* **Beltrami County:** Auditor-Treasurer's Office (701 Minnesota Ave NW, Ste 220, Bemidji, MN 56601). Open Mon–Fri 8:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m.
* **Lake of the Woods County** : Lake of the Woods Government Center (206 8th Ave SE, Baudette, MN 56623). Open Mon–Fri 7:30 a.m.–4:00 p.m.

If your voter registration is current and active, you do not need to bring identification. Your voter registration is considered active if you were registered at least 21 days before Election Day and you have not moved or changed names since then. If you need to register or update your registration, or you have not voted in four years or more, you will need to show [proof of residence](https://votereedolson.us/l/D45fnJxysT75) before you vote.
---
**📬 Early by Mail**
---
To vote by mail, apply to have an absentee ballot mailed to you. Your returned ballot must be received by Election Day. Find out more and apply on the [Secretary of State’s website](https://votereedolson.us/l/GZWuj5bwALV0).
---
|
---
Thanks for helping out! \- Reed Olson

name: emergency-response@uso.org
subject: FW: Urgent Support Needed
body:
Your support makes a critical difference in times of crisis.
We're making sure you saw this urgent update on our emergency response efforts after Hurricane Milton struck Florida on Wednesday.
**Thousands of National Guard members have received emergency deployment orders in the past three weeks** -- with Hurricane Helene recovery in the Southeast and response to Hurricane Milton in Florida.
[SUPPORT OUR HEROES NOW](https://links.e.uso.)
---
They're working around the clock to support affected communities at this urgent moment, and the USO is determined to be there with them every step of the way.
**[We missed our initial emergency-response goal of $50,000 to support our service members in this critical moment-- but we're extending our deadline to try to make up the gap. Please, will you rush an emergency donation of $29 or more to support our heroes and help us reach our $50,000 goal by midnight?*](https://links.e.uso.)**
--The USO
* * *
**From: **Emergency Response @ USO
**Sent: **Thursday, October 10, 2024
**Subject:** Hurricane Milton Update:
[](https://www.uso.org)
[GIVE NOW](https://links.e.uso.)
---
**BREAKING: Thousands of National Guard and active duty service members responding to Hurricane Milton need our support.** [**Will you rush an emergency donation of $29 or more to support our heroes around the world at this critical moment?***](https://links.e.uso.)
---
Last night, Hurricane Milton struck Florida as a Category 3 storm, bringing with it a massive storm surge, catastrophic tornadoes and devastating flooding.
While the worst of the damage is still being assessed and this is a rapidly developing situation, we know many of the affected communities were still recovering from Hurricane Helene less than two weeks ago, making this storm's impact even worse.
Thousands of National Guard members are still working to help communities recover from Hurricane Helene. Now, thousands more are being deployed to Florida from all over the country to conduct search and rescue missions, clear debris and provide lifesaving aid to communities in urgent need.
[**In times of increased need, the USO 's work to support and uplift service members is more important than ever -- but to scale up our work in moments of crisis, we rely on generous people like you. Please, will you give $29 or more now to support our heroes around the world at this urgent moment and into the future?**](https://links.e.uso.)
**[RUSH AN EMERGENCY DONATION](https://links.e.uso.)**
---
**The USO is the only nonprofit organization that goes wherever our service members do** -- from communities devastated by hurricanes, wildfires and other disasters across the United States to conflict zones around the world.
Right now, our teams are actively working to assess the needs of service members in Florida -- including National Guard members deployed in response to this emergency and military families stationed in the affected communities. We're ready to do whatever it takes to support them, from providing water and basic hygiene items to making sure they have the ability to connect with their loved ones.
**Your support makes all that and more possible, so please:**[**Will you rush $29 or more now to help reach our $50,000 rapid-response goal by midnight so we can support all of our heroes, including those responding to this emergency?**](https://links.e.uso.)
**[RUSH AN EMERGENCY DONATION](https://links.e.uso.org/els/v2/0d-ehpD_Kxfp/UWFYVjBWaDBwQmRySlFoNVpQYmFRVlF4YWdRYld2dDhReE9yT09uYythMm53ckZ2Rk4vcHVwZmM2UzRKMXFoOUhuczBrbnNoOGswY2lnMWpkbjJTYmx6bXNVUWp6bG9CWUtSVVFFelE3ZE09S0/cnF0Zkp0clFVRlYrd3dENThJbk9aQzg3ZWo0ek91ZGpmWEVxQjJtL2JKc0lyb0RCSGNIK2FraU9WcGoxRUEzR2dmd3pOd240WnNxTzN3ZFlMNS9NRStmL1I5N1BzOFFSS0)**
---
We'll continue to keep you updated as this ongoing situation develops -- for now, thank you for helping the USO be there for service members and their families when they need us most.
--The USO

subject: 🍵 The tea about yesterday’s DACA hearing:
body:
Hear more about it at our community call! Are you signed up yet? | | | Peter, hear me out: **🙄 Yesterday, anti-immigrant forces took to the Fifth Circuit Court to try to bring down DACA, again, and with it, our sense of safety and stability.__** Despite years of calculated attacks against our community, DACA has existed for over a decade**because** of our collective power and organizing! * **TOP NEWS**

"**Two dead, dozens injured after chemical release of hydrogen sulfide in Deer Park** ," Houston Landing's **Elena Bruess** -- "A chemical release at the Pemex refinery in Deer Park killed at least two people, injured several dozen, and prompted the issue of shelter-in-place orders for the Cities of Deer Park and Pasadena on Thursday night.

"We believe at this point that there are two persons deceased on scene," Harris County Sheriff **Ed Gonzalez** said. "We don't know if there could be more."

Gonzalez also explained that emergency personnel have not been able "to actually make entry into the unit itself because it's dynamic, and we want to render the area safe. That could take another 7 or 8 hours."

Another 35 workers were triaged for care at the facility, said Gonzalez, during a press conference Thursday night.

The incident occurred at 4:40 p.m. Thursday afternoon when Pemex employees were working on a flange at the facility, Gonzalez said.
[Give a gift subscription](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9tdXN0cmVhZHR4LnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.e2chMpw5641nqBmyJNlaSj6SpOI8BDDHFEPkhgSTZZA?&gift=true)
The chemical released is hydrogen sulfide, a colorless, flammable, toxic gas that is hazardous even in small amounts. It strongly smells of rotten eggs and can cause various health issues, from irritation to headaches to seizures.

"There are still some levels of this material that is a little bit elevated, but it's contained within the complex itself," Gonzalez said. "We want to make sure those levels are a little bit lower. We'd rather be cautious here rather than rushing in there and somebody else gets exposed."

There are no concerning levels of hydrogen sulfide in the community surrounding the facility, according to air monitoring conducted by Harris County Pollution Control and the City of Deer Park.

"There may be smells in the community still, but we have double-checked and verified that there's been no danger that we have been able to document that anything has gotten outside the complex," said Deer Park Mayor **Jerry Mouton**.

Early on Thursday evening, the emergency offices of Pasadena and Deer Park urged residents to close all windows and doors, turn off air conditioners, and wait until the all-clear had been issued out of precaution. Both municipalities lifted the shelter-in-place orders by 10 p.m.

"We are aware of the odor but there is no hazard to the community," the City of Deer Park said [via X](https://substack.com/redirect/b95d0e4a-98bb-4a10-a84f-e7e05267c2ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

Deer Park also noted [via X](https://substack.com/redirect/053b5334-d2b6-4708-939b-f753c552a57b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that their emergency text service is malfunctioning, and some residents may not receive alerts about the chemical release." [Houston Landing](https://substack.com/redirect/fed4bf17-e51d-4aa0-823b-4f91a073e243?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

"**Amber Guygen denied parole** ," Dallas Morning News' **Maggie Prosser** and **Kelli Smith** -- "Former Dallas police officer **Amber Guyger** , who was sentenced to 10 years in prison for the 2018 murder of **Botham Jean** , was denied parole Thursday, according to Jean's family.

Guyger, 36, [was eligible for parole late last month](https://substack.com/redirect/de8e662f-5ad2-4b55-aeac-3b90642fdb8a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) -- on what would have been Jean's 33rd birthday -- after serving half her sentence in a Gatesville prison. Jean's family, the Dallas County district attorney's office and [more than 6,300 people who signed an online petition](https://substack.com/redirect/7ffd25c0-ee52-4ba1-a659-e3576703e6ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) protested Guyger's parole.

Jean's sister, **Allisa Charles-Findley** , provided _The Dallas Morning News_ with an email notification from the Texas Department of Criminal Justice. According to the email, Guyger will be up for release again in 2026.

The email said, in part, "This is to notify you that the Texas Board of Pardons and Paroles denied parole for this offender." It also acknowledged the "criminal victimization" the family has experienced.

Allison Jean, Jean's mother, told _The News_ in a statement that her family "feels a sense of relief," adding it shows "part of the accountability that she must have for her actions." She has said she doesn't sense remorse from Guyger after previous failed appeals. Texas' highest criminal court upheld her conviction and the U.S. Supreme Court declined to review the case in 2022." [DMN](https://substack.com/redirect/c14a1cdc-2eaa-4bdb-8746-f25410a6aed8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ($)

"**Texas Ag Commissioner Sid Miller subpoenaed to testify in his former political consultant's criminal trial** ," Texas Tribune's **Juan Salinas II** -- "Texas Agriculture Commissioner **Sid Miller** was subpoenaed to testify in the criminal trial of one of his former political consultants later this month.

**Todd Smith** , a top aide for Miller, was indicted in 2022 on felony charges of theft and commercial bribery related to taking money in exchange for state hemp licenses that are issued by Miller's office.

Smith was arrested in mid-2021, accused by law enforcement of taking $55,000 as part of the scheme, [according to an arrest warrant](https://substack.com/redirect/16d5e12e-8dfd-4138-851b-512669eed287?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Smith and others were accused of soliciting up to $150,000 to guarantee an "exclusive" hemp license from the Texas Department of Agriculture. Smith allegedly said $25,000 of that money would be used for a survey that he said was required to get a license in Texas. A hemp license from the state costs $100, according to the arrest warrant.

Miller could not be immediately reached for comment. At the time of the indictment, Miller suggested it was politically motivated and said he didn't believe Smith did anything wrong.

Miller is ordered to testify in a Travis County District Court on Oct. 21." [Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/6489ff7e-708f-4d89-932c-eb176bf8d0dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
* **BUSINESS NEWS**

**Jason Wells op ed:** "**CenterPoint CEO: I apologize. Houston's grid will be better** ," Houston Chronicle's**Jason Wells ** -- "I'm the president and CEO of CenterPoint. During the recent Public Utility Commission of Texas hearing in Houston, as well as other forums this summer, we heard loud and clear that our response to Hurricane Beryl was unacceptable and did not meet our customers' and communities' expectations. Our customers were frustrated because the number of outages was too high, the length of outages was too long and our communications did not meet their expectations or our own.

I want to personally apologize to each and every one of our customers for the pain and frustration they experienced, and I want to reiterate that we at CenterPoint are more resolved than ever to make sure that the frustration they experienced never happens again. Both our leadership team and our dedicated workforce are acting with a sense of urgency to re-earn trust and build the most resilient coastal grid in the country.

Two months ago, we launched a multiphase [Greater Houston Resiliency Initiative](https://substack.com/redirect/2516e0bb-61c3-4f2b-bffe-6595bf54022f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (GHRI), which included a broad range of actions to address our customers' concerns and strengthen the resiliency of our electric system; improve our customer and public communications; and develop stronger partnerships with community and emergency preparedness leaders.

The [first phase of GHRI](https://substack.com/redirect/de55825e-0cd7-4cb2-b9ba-fbcf89796246?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which launched in early August, included installing over 1,100 new poles capable of withstanding extreme winds; removing higher-risk vegetation from over 2,000 miles of power lines; and installing over 300 automated devices that help to reduce the length of outages. The initial phase of GHRI, which was focused on improving resiliency for the remainder of the 2024 hurricane season, was [completed ahead of schedule](https://substack.com/redirect/de55825e-0cd7-4cb2-b9ba-fbcf89796246?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). But we clearly realize that more needs to be done to build a more reliable and resilient grid.

To hear directly from our customers about what matters most, we conducted 19 [community open house events](https://substack.com/redirect/49b8cf44-0197-49d1-a7f0-dd98800c5ad5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) across all 12 counties in our Greater Houston service area. We also reached out extensively to elected officials, regulators and emergency preparedness experts. This collective feedback was invaluable. Going forward, we are committed to seeking feedback and partnering with the communities we are privileged to serve.

In early September we launched [the next phase of GHRI](https://substack.com/redirect/1f583382-b25c-4131-8ec3-f4d563f68e27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which will further improve resiliency and build on the progress made during Phase One. This second phase of GHRI, expected to be finished June 1, includes:

> Installing or replacing 25,000 poles that meet our enhanced extreme wind standards;
> Trimming or removing higher-risk vegetation across 4,000 miles of power lines;
> Installing 4,500 automation devices and 350 [Intelligent Grid Switching Devices](https://substack.com/redirect/dd1e1851-618a-4076-809f-36947a1c1af5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as part of our efforts to build a self-healing grid, which will reduce the frequency and duration of outages; and
> Undergrounding more than 400 miles of power lines.

Once completed, we expect these resiliency actions to reduce customer-outage minutes by approximately 125 million per year.

We aim to continue to keep the public informed in an open and transparent way about our progress and next steps. To that end, we have launched an online progress dashboard, which you can visit at [CenterPointEnergy.com/TakingAction](https://substack.com/redirect/7203599c-296b-4e62-9a89-886bd965c94f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). We will provide regular updates on the scope of GHRI work being completed all over Houston.

All of us at CenterPoint fully recognize the pivotal role the Greater Houston area plays. Our region is one of the most rapidly growing cities in the nation, the economic engine of Texas and the energy capital of the world. That's why we are so determined to get this right.

We know that words alone will not be enough to re-earn our customers' trust. Our customers must see real improvement. Actions are what we will deliver. To that end, we will remain laser-focused on what is most important: delivering actions and results and re-earning your trust by building a grid that will serve our region's needs for years to come.

_Jason Wells is president and CEO of CenterPoint. " _[Houston Chronicle](https://substack.com/redirect/1bb2e4f8-24a8-4240-a28e-f92ae0210f99?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ($)

The company also expects to make the Full Self-Driving technology available on its popular Model 3 and Model Y vehicles in Texas and California next year.

"**Ken Paxton's voter registration suit against Travis County returned to state court** ," Texas Tribune's **Kayla Guo** -- "A federal court on Thursday returned a lawsuit to state court that Texas Attorney General **Ken Paxton** had filed against Travis County over an effort to register voters before the November election.

The federal court found that it did not have jurisdiction over the issue, as Travis County officials had argued, and it granted Paxton's request that the lawsuit be returned to state court.

The decision is the latest development in a bitter pre-election brawl between Republican state officials and Democratic county leaders. Republican leaders have maintained that they are trying to keep the state's voter rolls secure ahead of a charged election, while Democrats, county officials and nonprofit groups have accused them of stoking baseless fears to suppress Democratic votes and to cast doubt on the election results.

Here's what you need to know.

**The background:** In a bid to boost voter registrations, Travis County commissioners hired Civic Government Solutions in August to identify eligible voters living in the county who were not registered to vote. Travis County, a Democratic stronghold, includes Austin.

[Paxton sued Travis County officials](https://substack.com/redirect/275dcf44-0994-4a2c-84a2-3bc3732b49fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Sept. 5, arguing that the effort violated state law and claiming that it would register non-citizens who are ineligible to vote. He sought an emergency order to block the effort. The Travis County Court denied his request on Sept. 16.

The next day, Travis County officials moved the suit to federal court, arguing that the voter outreach program was protected by the federal National Voter Registration Act, and that Paxton's attempt to stop it was a violation of that law. County officials also sued Paxton for the same reason in a separate lawsuit in federal court.

Thursday's decision said that the National Voter Registration Act was meant to be applied in tandem with state law, and that Travis County officials failed to show that the issue fell under the federal court's jurisdiction.

**Why Texas sued:** In suing Travis County officials in September, Paxton called the decision by county commissioners to hire an outside firm and move forward with the voter outreach program illegal.

"Travis County has blatantly violated Texas law by paying partisan actors to conduct unlawful identification efforts to track down people who are not registered to vote," Paxton said at the time. "Programs like this invite fraud and reduce public trust in our elections. We will stop them and any other county considering such programs."

Paxton, without evidence, has routinely accused Democrats of adopting more permissive immigration policies to boost the ranks of noncitizens to vote and help them win elections. Only U.S. citizens are permitted to vote under both federal and state law. Data shows that instances of noncitizen voting are exceedingly rare.

**What Travis County said:** Travis County officials defended their work to register eligible voters and accused Paxton of violating a federal law that protects voter outreach programs.

"Travis County is committed to encouraging voter participation and we are proud of our outreach efforts that achieve higher voter registration numbers," county spokesperson **Hector Nieto** said in September. "We remain steadfast in our responsibility to uphold the integrity of the voter registration process while ensuring that every eligible person has the opportunity to exercise their right to vote. It is disappointing that any statewide elected official would prefer to sow distrust and discourage participation in the electoral process."

At The Texas Tribune Festival in September, Travis County Judge **Andy Brown** said that county officials should do all they could to register voters, particularly in a state where residents cannot register online. "Paxton does this every time," Brown said.

**Jeremy Smith** , Civic Government Solutions' chief executive, said that outreach efforts would be strictly nonpartisan and would pose little risk of registering noncitizens. He said that the company uses a mix of public records and county data to identify people who could have recently moved and are unregistered, and he noted various checks in place to prevent noncitizens from registering to vote.

When voter registrars receive applications, they send them to the Texas Secretary of State's Office, where they are checked for eligibility against Department of Public Safety and Social Security Administration data. In addition, local voter registrars work with their county district attorney's office to check citizenship status using responses from jury summons questionnaires.

In a separate, [federal lawsuit filed on Sept. 17](https://substack.com/redirect/ec2443c3-4c46-40e6-b560-ee6d4f764818?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Travis County officials accused Paxton and Texas Secretary of State Jane Nelson of violating the federal Voting Rights Act by trying to prevent them from carrying out their duty to promote people's right to vote. They accused Nelson of doing nothing to stop Paxton's alleged conduct, and they argued that federal law not only allows them to send out the voter registration applications, but encourages them to do so." [Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/a777e227-8bd7-40e7-a590-e1471af519d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

"**ERCOT likely to force CPS Energy to keep Braunig plants open** ," San Antonio Express-News' **Sara DiNatale** -- "CPS Energy is facing the likelihood the state grid operator will force it to keep its aging gas-fired generating plants at the Braunig Power Station running past their proposed March retirement.

The [city-owned utility](https://substack.com/redirect/38927154-ec64-4149-9d7a-58187a95a3e6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) wants to shut down the three 60-year-old plants, which it says can no longer be run without major expenses. Because they're situated near a trouble spot in the state's transmission infrastructure, though, the Electric Reliability Council of Texas says their loss would heighten the risk of cascading outages to the entire grid.

ERCOT [tried for the past few months](https://substack.com/redirect/7220edf7-0d7e-45fa-b63d-5e62e9d13f48?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to find enough power to replace Braunig's output of 849 megawatts but got little industry response. Only one application was received by a Monday deadline -- a battery storage site offering 200 megawatts when it opens in 2026.

"That's a little disappointing that we weren't able to get more interest from the industry to respond, because ... the consumers of Texas will ultimately have to pay for any type of solution," ERCOT General Counsel **Chad Seely** told board members Thursday.

That leaves ERCOT to weigh what it will take to keep the plants running against the costs of resorting to controlled outages in the face of transmission issues Braunig's current output helps mitigate.

The options could include using all or none of the Braunig units along with the proposed new battery site. The grid operator plans to ask its board of directors to vote on a plan in December.

CPS has put the cost to keep the plans running at as much as $200 million, which would ultimately be paid by ratepayers across Texas.

The analysis requires shutting down the plants for a planned 60-day inspection process. CPS agreed to move up the largest unit's outage by three weeks to March 2 to get a head start on the inspection process. Originally, CPS had planned to decommission the plant on March 31.

ERCOT previously considered paying millions of dollars to CPS to close the plants this winter for early inspections but later determined that would put the grid at too much risk when power demand peaks during seasonal cold snaps." "**Austin Police Department set to begin DWI no-refusal initiative year-round** ," Austin American-Statesman's **Skye Seipp** -- "For the first time, the Austin Police Department is moving its no-refusal program for suspected impaired driving to be every day, year-round, rather than something done on holiday weekends or during other special events.

The change comes after a summer initiative when the department began its no-refusal program every day. During no-refusal periods, officers can more easily obtain search warrants for blood or breath samples from impaired driving suspects who refuse to willingly provide samples.

Police Detective **Jason Day** said no-refusal is valuable because it allows police to get the evidence they need to help increase the chances of prosecution. Day added that the summer initiative led to the department seeing a 30% increase in warrants this year compared with last.

"We want people to get out and enjoy the community," Day said during a news conference Thursday. "But we want to make sure they have a plan and a safe ride home."

When Day first started on the force, he said, there weren't enough taxis for people to safely get home. But with the advent of ride-hailing service apps such as Uber, he said people have "no excuse" for driving impaired.

To obtain a warrant, police must present enough evidence to a municipal judge that the person was driving under the influence of drugs or alcohol. Day said the initiative is not a "rubber stamp," and that officers will still have to meet certain expectations for a judge to sign off on a warrant.

As part of the no-refusal effort, Day said every night there will be a DWI expert at the jail to help officers in all their DWI cases, whether the suspect is refusing or not.

In cases where a person suspected of a DWI refuses to give a breath or blood sample, Day said the expert will be there to help make the process of getting a warrant more efficient. About 40% of people stopped in Austin for a suspected DWI refuse to give a sample, Day said.

While the no-refusal program will operate every day, it will only take place at night from 9 p.m. to 5 a.m., the time when 70% of DWIs take place, Day said." "**More principals left Fort Worth ISD last year than in any year since 2017** ," Fort Worth Report's **Matthew Sgroi** -- "More principals left Fort Worth ISD last school year than in any other year since at least 2017, according to data from two open records requests filed by the Fort Worth Report.

Educators say that the exit of a principal can lead to a lack of stability that students expect when they arrive on campus each day. The role includes building relationships with teachers and fostering connections between parents and school staff.

Families are used to seeing the same faces in their schools when they drop their kids off and pick them up, said **Steven Poole** , director of the United Educators Association.

"It causes some discomfort at the parent level," Poole said. "They want stability in their schools, they want to know that the principals are there, and will be there, in their school."

When a break occurs, campus resources are strained, Poole said. That stress has been increasingly felt by parents and educators across Fort Worth ISD in the past year, according to Poole [and several teachers](https://substack.com/redirect/aea41b61-406e-42a3-bc3b-19e590281717?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). During the 2023-24 school year, 49 principals or assistant principals across 41 campuses resigned or retired.

These numbers mark an increase from previous years, as an average of 34 principals and assistant principals left annually since 2017. Interim Superintendent **Karen Molinar** and her administration, who are taking over following Superintendent **Ang elica Ramsey's** [two-year tenure](https://substack.com/redirect/f3a6e38b-b600-4af8-a5a5-950795dc4d2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), must focus on retaining their most experienced educators before they leave or retire early, Poole said.

"Principals don't quit their schools, they quit their districts," Poole said. "That's what I've heard from a lot of principals who have left Fort Worth ISD. They're frustrated."" That same day, U.S. House Speaker **Mike Johnson** - in Arlington to launch his national American Revival Tour - proclaimed Texas as the linchpin of the 2024 election.

That was a lot of political muscle flexing in the county of 2.1 million people.

The vote in Tarrant County could play a significant role in determining whether Cruz remains in the Senate or Allred can become the first Democrat to win a statewide race in 30 years. Election returns also will be watched to see if the county remains its current shade of light red or shifts to a shade closer to blue.

Cruz and Allred stressed the importance of winning Tarrant County and other North Texas areas.

"This is a battle between sane and crazy," Cruz said at Outpost 36 BBQ in Keller. "This race is about keeping Texas, Texas."

Allred said Texans face a critical choice.

"We've got one month, one month to stand up for the state that we know we are," he said at Tulips FTW.

Democrats and Republicans echo the call.

"Tarrant County is in a precarious position," said Tarrant County Republican Party Chairman **Bo French** at the Cruz rally. "I'm gonna tell you, we have a lot of work to do."

"Tarrant County is truly the biggest battleground in the state of Texas," said state Rep. **Chris Turner** , D-Grand Prairie, at Allred's gathering.

"This is going to be a close race, and so every vote is going to count," Turner said of the Allred-Cruz showdown. "And if I tell you we win Tarrant County ... ($5/mo or $50/yr or $199 lifetime) TOP NEWS "Two dead, dozens injured after chemical release of hydrogen sulfide in Deer Park ," Houston Landing's Elena Bruess -- "A chemical release at the Pemex refinery in Deer Park killed at least two people, injured several dozen, and prompted the issue of shelter-in-place orders for the Cities of Deer Park and Pasadena on Thursday night. "We believe at this point that there are two persons deceased on scene," Harris County Sheriff Ed Gonzalez said. "We don't know if there could be more." Gonzalez also explained that emergency personnel have not been able "to actually make entry into the unit itself because it's dynamic, and we want to render the area safe. That could take another 7 or 8 hours." Another 35 workers were triaged for care at the facility, said Gonzalez, during a press conference Thursday night. The incident occurred at 4:40 p.m. Thursday afternoon when Pemex employees were working on a flange at the facility, Gonzalez said. The chemical released is hydrogen sulfide, a colorless, flammable, toxic gas that is hazardous even in small amounts. It strongly smells of rotten eggs and can cause various health issues, from irritation to headaches to seizures. "There are still some levels of this material that is a little bit elevated, but it's contained within the complex itself," Gonzalez said. "We want to make sure those levels are a little bit lower. We'd rather be cautious here rather than rushing in there and somebody else gets exposed." There are no concerning levels of hydrogen sulfide in the community surrounding the facility, according to air monitoring conducted by Harris County Pollution Control and the City of Deer Park. "There may be smells in the community still, but we have double-checked and verified that there's been no danger that we have been able to document that anything has gotten outside the complex," said Deer Park Mayor Jerry Mouton. Early on Thursday evening, the emergency offices of Pasadena and Deer Park urged residents to close all windows and doors, turn off air conditioners, and wait until the all-clear had been issued out of precaution. Both municipalities lifted the shelter-in-place orders by 10 p.m. "We are aware of the odor but there is no hazard to the community," the City of Deer Park said . Deer Park also noted that their emergency text service is malfunctioning, and some residents may not receive alerts about the chemical release." "Amber Guygen denied parole ," Dallas Morning News' Maggie Prosser and Kelli Smith -- "Former Dallas police officer Amber Guyger , who was sentenced to 10 years in prison for the 2018 murder of Botham Jean , was denied parole Thursday, according to Jean's family. Guyger, 36, -- on what would have been Jean's 33rd birthday -- after serving half her sentence in a Gatesville prison. Jean's family, the Dallas County district attorney's office and protested Guyger's parole. Jean's sister, Allisa Charles-Findley , provided The Dallas Morning News with an email notification from the Texas Department of Criminal Justice. According to the email, Guyger will be up for release again in 2026. The email said, in part, "This is to notify you that the Texas Board of Pardons and Paroles denied parole for this offender." It also acknowledged the "criminal victimization" the family has experienced. Allison Jean, Jean's mother, told The News in a statement that her family "feels a sense of relief," adding it shows "part of the accountability that she must have for her actions." She has said she doesn't sense remorse from Guyger after previous failed appeals. Texas' highest criminal court upheld her conviction and the U.S. Supreme Court declined to review the case in 2022." ($) "Texas Ag Commissioner Sid Miller subpoenaed to testify in his former political consultant's criminal trial ," Texas Tribune's Juan Salinas II -- "Texas Agriculture Commissioner Sid Miller was subpoenaed to testify in the criminal trial of one of his former political consultants later this month. Todd Smith , a top aide for Miller, was indicted in 2022 on felony charges of theft and commercial bribery related to taking money in exchange for state hemp licenses that are issued by Miller's office. Smith was arrested in mid-2021, accused by law enforcement of taking $55,000 as part of the scheme, . Smith and others were accused of soliciting up to $150,000 to guarantee an "exclusive" hemp license from the Texas Department of Agriculture. Smith allegedly said $25,000 of that money would be used for a survey that he said was required to get a license in Texas. A hemp license from the state costs $100, according to the arrest warrant. Miller could not be immediately reached for comment. At the time of the indictment, Miller suggested it was politically motivated and said he didn't believe Smith did anything wrong. Miller is ordered to testify in a Travis County District Court on Oct. 21." BUSINESS NEWS Jason Wells op ed: "CenterPoint CEO: I apologize. Houston's grid will be better ," Houston Chronicle'sJason Wells -- "I'm the president and CEO of CenterPoint. During the recent Public Utility Commission of Texas hearing in Houston, as well as other forums this summer, we heard loud and clear that our response to Hurricane Beryl was unacceptable and did not meet our customers' and communities' expectations. Our customers were frustrated because the number of outages was too high, the length of outages was too long and our communications did not meet their expectations or our own. I want to personally apologize to each and every one of our customers for the pain and frustration they experienced, and I want to reiterate that we at CenterPoint are more resolved than ever to make sure that the frustration they experienced never happens again. Both our leadership team and our dedicated workforce are acting with a sense of urgency to re-earn trust and build the most resilient coastal grid in the country. Two months ago, we launched a multiphase (GHRI), which included a broad range of actions to address our customers' concerns and strengthen the resiliency of our electric system; improve our customer and public communications; and develop stronger partnerships with community and emergency preparedness leaders. The , which launched in early August, included installing over 1,100 new poles capable of withstanding extreme winds; removing higher-risk vegetation from over 2,000 miles of power lines; and installing over 300 automated devices that help to reduce the length of outages. The initial phase of GHRI, which was focused on improving resiliency for the remainder of the 2024 hurricane season, was . But we clearly realize that more needs to be done to build a more reliable and resilient grid. To hear directly from our customers about what matters most, we conducted 19 across all 12 counties in our Greater Houston service area. We also reached out extensively to elected officials, regulators and emergency preparedness experts. This collective feedback was invaluable. Going forward, we are committed to seeking feedback and partnering with the communities we are privileged to serve. In early September we launched , which will further improve resiliency and build on the progress made during Phase One. This second phase of GHRI, expected to be finished June 1, includes: Installing or replacing 25,000 poles that meet our enhanced extreme wind standards; Trimming or removing higher-risk vegetation across 4,000 miles of power lines; Installing 4,500 automation devices and 350 as part of our efforts to build a self-healing grid, which will reduce the frequency and duration of outages; and Undergrounding more than 400 miles of power lines. Once completed, we expect these resiliency actions to reduce customer-outage minutes by approximately 125 million per year. We aim to continue to keep the public informed in an open and transparent way about our progress and next steps. To that end, we have launched an online progress dashboard, which you can visit at . We will provide regular updates on the scope of GHRI work being completed all over Houston. All of us at CenterPoint fully recognize the pivotal role the Greater Houston area plays. Our region is one of the most rapidly growing cities in the nation, the economic engine of Texas and the energy capital of the world. That's why we are so determined to get this right. We know that words alone will not be enough to re-earn our customers' trust. Our customers must see real improvement. Actions are what we will deliver. To that end, we will remain laser-focused on what is most important: delivering actions and results and re-earning your trust by building a grid that will serve our region's needs for years to come. Jason Wells is president and CEO of CenterPoint. " ($) "Musk unveils Tesla's 'Cybercab,' autonomous driving to Texas ," San Antonio Express-News'Tom Krisher andAlex Veiga -- "Tesla Inc. unveiled its long-awaited robotaxi at a Hollywood studio Thursday night, though fans of the Texas-based electric vehicle maker will have to wait until at least 2026 before they are available. CEO Elon Musk pulled up to a stage at the Warner Bros. studio lot in one of ," telling the crowd that the sleek, AI-powered vehicles don't have steering wheels or pedals. He also expressed confidence in the progress the company has made on autonomous driving technology that makes it possible for vehicles to drive without human intervention. Tesla began selling the software, which is called "Full Self-Driving," nine years ago. But there are . "We'll move from supervised Full Self-Driving to unsupervised Full Self-Driving. where you can fall asleep and wake up at your destination," he said. "It's going to be a glorious future." Tesla expects the Cybercabs to cost less than $30,000, Musk said. He estimated that the vehicles would become available in 2026, then added "before 2027." The company also expects to make the Full Self-Driving technology available on its popular Model 3 and Model Y vehicles in Texas and California next year. "If they're going to eventually get to robotaxis, they first need to have success with the unsupervised FSD at the current lineup," said Seth Goldstein , equity strategist at Morningstar Research. "Tonight's event showed that they're ready to take that step forward." When Tesla will actually take that step, however, has led to more than a little anxiety for investors who see other automakers deploying similar technology right now. Shares of Tesla Inc. tumbled almost 7% before the opening bell Friday." ($) STATE GOVERNMENT "Ken Paxton's voter registration suit against Travis County returned to state court ," Texas Tribune's Kayla Guo -- "A federal court on Thursday returned a lawsuit to state court that Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton had filed against Travis County over an effort to register voters before the November election. The federal court found that it did not have jurisdiction over the issue, as Travis County officials had argued, and it granted Paxton's request that the lawsuit be returned to state court. The decision is the latest development in a bitter pre-election brawl between Republican state officials and Democratic county leaders. Republican leaders have maintained that they are trying to keep the state's voter rolls secure ahead of a charged election, while Democrats, county officials and nonprofit groups have accused them of stoking baseless fears to suppress Democratic votes and to cast doubt on the election results. Here's what you need to know. The background: In a bid to boost voter registrations, Travis County commissioners hired Civic Government Solutions in August to identify eligible voters living in the county who were not registered to vote. Travis County, a Democratic stronghold, includes Austin. on Sept. 5, arguing that the effort violated state law and claiming that it would register non-citizens who are ineligible to vote. He sought an emergency order to block the effort. The Travis County Court denied his request on Sept. 16. The next day, Travis County officials moved the suit to federal court, arguing that the voter outreach program was protected by the federal National Voter Registration Act, and that Paxton's attempt to stop it was a violation of that law. County officials also sued Paxton for the same reason in a separate lawsuit in federal court. Thursday's decision said that the National Voter Registration Act was meant to be applied in tandem with state law, and that Travis County officials failed to show that the issue fell under the federal court's jurisdiction. Why Texas sued: In suing Travis County officials in September, Paxton called the decision by county commissioners to hire an outside firm and move forward with the voter outreach program illegal. "Travis County has blatantly violated Texas law by paying partisan actors to conduct unlawful identification efforts to track down people who are not registered to vote," Paxton said at the time. "Programs like this invite fraud and reduce public trust in our elections. We will stop them and any other county considering such programs." Paxton, without evidence, has routinely accused Democrats of adopting more permissive immigration policies to boost the ranks of noncitizens to vote and help them win elections. Only U.S. citizens are permitted to vote under both federal and state law. Data shows that instances of noncitizen voting are exceedingly rare. What Travis County said: Travis County officials defended their work to register eligible voters and accused Paxton of violating a federal law that protects voter outreach programs. "Travis County is committed to encouraging voter participation and we are proud of our outreach efforts that achieve higher voter registration numbers," county spokesperson Hector Nieto said in September. "We remain steadfast in our responsibility to uphold the integrity of the voter registration process while ensuring that every eligible person has the opportunity to exercise their right to vote. It is disappointing that any statewide elected official would prefer to sow distrust and discourage participation in the electoral process." At The Texas Tribune Festival in September, Travis County Judge Andy Brown said that county officials should do all they could to register voters, particularly in a state where residents cannot register online. "Paxton does this every time," Brown said. Jeremy Smith , Civic Government Solutions' chief executive, said that outreach efforts would be strictly nonpartisan and would pose little risk of registering noncitizens. He said that the company uses a mix of public records and county data to identify people who could have recently moved and are unregistered, and he noted various checks in place to prevent noncitizens from registering to vote. When voter registrars receive applications, they send them to the Texas Secretary of State's Office, where they are checked for eligibility against Department of Public Safety and Social Security Administration data. In addition, local voter registrars work with their county district attorney's office to check citizenship status using responses from jury summons questionnaires. In a separate, , Travis County officials accused Paxton and Texas Secretary of State Jane Nelson of violating the federal Voting Rights Act by trying to prevent them from carrying out their duty to promote people's right to vote. They accused Nelson of doing nothing to stop Paxton's alleged conduct, and they argued that federal law not only allows them to send out the voter registration applications, but encourages them to do so." "ERCOT likely to force CPS Energy to keep Braunig plants open ," San Antonio Express-News' Sara DiNatale -- "CPS Energy is facing the likelihood the state grid operator will force it to keep its aging gas-fired generating plants at the Braunig Power Station running past their proposed March retirement. The wants to shut down the three 60-year-old plants, which it says can no longer be run without major expenses. Because they're situated near a trouble spot in the state's transmission infrastructure, though, the Electric Reliability Council of Texas says their loss would heighten the risk of cascading outages to the entire grid. ERCOT to find enough power to replace Braunig's output of 849 megawatts but got little industry response. Only one application was received by a Monday deadline -- a battery storage site offering 200 megawatts when it opens in 2026. "That's a little disappointing that we weren't able to get more interest from the industry to respond, because ... the consumers of Texas will ultimately have to pay for any type of solution," ERCOT General Counsel Chad Seely told board members Thursday. That leaves ERCOT to weigh what it will take to keep the plants running against the costs of resorting to controlled outages in the face of transmission issues Braunig's current output helps mitigate. The options could include using all or none of the Braunig units along with the proposed new battery site. The grid operator plans to ask its board of directors to vote on a plan in December. CPS has put the cost to keep the plans running at as much as $200 million, which would ultimately be paid by ratepayers across Texas. The analysis requires shutting down the plants for a planned 60-day inspection process. CPS agreed to move up the largest unit's outage by three weeks to March 2 to get a head start on the inspection process. Originally, CPS had planned to decommission the plant on March 31. ERCOT previously considered paying millions of dollars to CPS to close the plants this winter for early inspections but later determined that would put the grid at too much risk when power demand peaks during seasonal cold snaps." ($) LOCAL GOVERNMENT "Three former Harris County Tax Office employees indicted for bribery ," Houston Chronicle's John Lomax V -- "Three former employees of the Harris County Tax Office were indicted on bribery charges, according to a statement released by Harris County Tax Assessor Ann Harris Bennett. While the employees were not named in the release, the charges stemmed from alleged fraud within the office's Automobile and Compliance Department. One employee was terminated, while the other two had resigned a year before. In a post on X, Precinct 4 Constable Mark Herman announced that deputies had arrested a former clerk on bribery charges. Court documents filed with the Harris County District Clerk's Office Tuesday accused Diana Flores-Cibrian of accepting cash payments between May 1, 2022, and June 8, 2023, from Arnold's Title Services LLC in exchange for processing transactions containing false information and processing titles in violation of Harris County Tax Office policy. Also listed in charging documents are two other individuals, identified only as "C. Gonzalez ," and "M. Martinez." "All Harris County residents should be assured that the Tax Office maintains a high level of internal controls and procedures to guarantee that all transactions are conducted in accordance with all state laws," Bennett said in a Thursday evening news release. "I remain proud of my staff and am grateful to those who discovered the crimes committed by these individuals, ultimately upholding the public's trust in everything we do." Bennett said once her office became aware of the alleged fraudulent activity, they immediately notified the Texas Comptroller's Office, the Harris County Precinct 1 Constable's Office and the Harris County District Attorney's Office, who opened an investigation into the matter." ($) "Austin Police Department set to begin DWI no-refusal initiative year-round ," Austin American-Statesman's Skye Seipp -- "For the first time, the Austin Police Department is moving its no-refusal program for suspected impaired driving to be every day, year-round, rather than something done on holiday weekends or during other special events. The change comes after a summer initiative when the department began its no-refusal program every day. During no-refusal periods, officers can more easily obtain search warrants for blood or breath samples from impaired driving suspects who refuse to willingly provide samples. Police Detective Jason Day said no-refusal is valuable because it allows police to get the evidence they need to help increase the chances of prosecution. Day added that the summer initiative led to the department seeing a 30% increase in warrants this year compared with last. "We want people to get out and enjoy the community," Day said during a news conference Thursday. "But we want to make sure they have a plan and a safe ride home." When Day first started on the force, he said, there weren't enough taxis for people to safely get home. But with the advent of ride-hailing service apps such as Uber, he said people have "no excuse" for driving impaired. To obtain a warrant, police must present enough evidence to a municipal judge that the person was driving under the influence of drugs or alcohol. Day said the initiative is not a "rubber stamp," and that officers will still have to meet certain expectations for a judge to sign off on a warrant. As part of the no-refusal effort, Day said every night there will be a DWI expert at the jail to help officers in all their DWI cases, whether the suspect is refusing or not. In cases where a person suspected of a DWI refuses to give a breath or blood sample, Day said the expert will be there to help make the process of getting a warrant more efficient. About 40% of people stopped in Austin for a suspected DWI refuse to give a sample, Day said. While the no-refusal program will operate every day, it will only take place at night from 9 p.m. to 5 a.m., the time when 70% of DWIs take place, Day said." ($) "More principals left Fort Worth ISD last year than in any year since 2017 ," Fort Worth Report's Matthew Sgroi -- "More principals left Fort Worth ISD last school year than in any other year since at least 2017, according to data from two open records requests filed by the Fort Worth Report. Educators say that the exit of a principal can lead to a lack of stability that students expect when they arrive on campus each day. The role includes building relationships with teachers and fostering connections between parents and school staff. Families are used to seeing the same faces in their schools when they drop their kids off and pick them up, said Steven Poole , director of the United Educators Association. "It causes some discomfort at the parent level," Poole said. "They want stability in their schools, they want to know that the principals are there, and will be there, in their school." When a break occurs, campus resources are strained, Poole said. That stress has been increasingly felt by parents and educators across Fort Worth ISD in the past year, according to Poole . During the 2023-24 school year, 49 principals or assistant principals across 41 campuses resigned or retired. These numbers mark an increase from previous years, as an average of 34 principals and assistant principals left annually since 2017. Interim Superintendent Karen Molinar and her administration, who are taking over following Superintendent Ang elica Ramsey's , must focus on retaining their most experienced educators before they leave or retire early, Poole said. "Principals don't quit their schools, they quit their districts," Poole said. "That's what I've heard from a lot of principals who have left Fort Worth ISD. They're frustrated."" "Tarrant County emerges as critical battleground in 2024 election ," Dallas Morning News' Gromer Jeffers, Jr. -- "With the U.S. Senate race pitting Colin Allred against Ted Cruz leading the fight, Tarrant County is one of the most important political battlegrounds in Texas. Once a reliable source of Republican votes, Dallas' western neighbor is a , particularly as new arrivals are making the area more diverse and politically unpredictable. The county's prominence was on display last Saturday, with Republicans and Democrats holding dueling events to launch the final month of campaigning before the Nov. 5 election. Cruz rallied GOP supporters at a Keller barbecue restaurant, while Allred joined Democrats for a rally at a Fort Worth honky tonk. That same day, U.S. House Speaker Mike Johnson - in Arlington to launch his national American Revival Tour - proclaimed Texas as the linchpin of the 2024 election. That was a lot of political muscle flexing in the county of 2.1 million people. The vote in Tarrant County could play a significant role in determining whether Cruz remains in the Senate or Allred can become the first Democrat to win a statewide race in 30 years. Election returns also will be watched to see if the county remains its current shade of light red or shifts to a shade closer to blue. Cruz and Allred stressed the importance of winning Tarrant County and other North Texas areas. "This is a battle between sane and crazy," Cruz said at Outpost 36 BBQ in Keller. "This race is about keeping Texas, Texas." Allred said Texans face a critical choice. "We've got one month, one month to stand up for the state that we know we are," he said at Tulips FTW. Democrats and Republicans echo the call. "Tarrant County is in a precarious position," said Tarrant County Republican Party Chairman Bo French at the Cruz rally. "I'm gonna tell you, we have a lot of work to do." "Tarrant County is truly the biggest battleground in the state of Texas," said state Rep. Chris Turner , D-Grand Prairie, at Allred's gathering. "This is going to be a close race, and so every vote is going to count," Turner said of the Allred-Cruz showdown. "And if I tell you we win Tarrant County ... I believe we will have elected Colin Allred the next U.S. senator from the state of Texas."" ($) 2024 "Did Gov. Abbott's primary meddling put a Northside house district in jeopardy for the GOP ," San Antonio Report's Andrea Drusch -- "Texas Democrats had largely abandoned their long-held dream of flipping House District 121 -- until Gov.Greg Abbott 's school voucher campaign thrust it back into the spotlight this year. Now an unlikely coalition of public education supporters, including House Democratic leaders, the state teachers' union and even Rep. Steve Allison (R-Alamo Heights) -- the ousted Republican incumbent -- are working together to help little-known Democrat Laurel Jordan Swift in her uphill race against conservative Marc LaHood , a voucher supporter who . The group's urgency was on full display Wednesday night, as state Reps. Gina Hinojosa(D-Austin), James Talarico (D-Austin), and House District 121's soon-to-be-former state Rep. Allison all huddled in San Antonio for a public education forum Swift hosted with state Rep. Diego Bernal (D-San Antonio). In a highly unusual move, Allison, when he a school voucher program last November, unabashedly joined the Democrats' call for a cross-party effort to stop the use of taxpayers funds for private school tuition at all costs. He called out Abbott, suggesting that the governor may have overplayed his hand when he aimed at fellow Republicans in the name of his school voucher plan earlier this year. "We can't lose sight of the big picture... we've got to protect public education," Allison said to the room of mainly San Antonio-area educators. "The governor thinks he has the votes [on vouchers]... and this election is one of those key three to five [seats] to flip that's going to make all the difference in the world." In an interview after the event, Allison, a former Alamo Heights ISD board president who has represented the district since 2018, said he believes Swift now has a real chance at a seat that's long eluded Democrats. "I'm supporting her, and urging others to do the same," said Allison, who still counts himself as a Republican." name: Robert F. Kennedy Jr.
subject: Thank you for the outpouring of support
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY TEAM KENNEDY
body:
|

[](https://www.kennedy24.com?e=d33e868971601c1c714cfe0555abd394&utm_source=joinkennedy&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=ethel_10_11_24_all_1&n=1)
Peter,
Thank you for the outpouring of support in response to my mother's passing. I wanted to share with you the tribute I wrote and posted on social media yesterday.
[](https://www.mahanow.org/r?u=GNKpkpGYUOJ5IEOpH8lWzi3WoTjl5qlJj0qsxmTzTfs&e=d33e868971601c1c714cfe0555abd394&utm_source=joinkennedy&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=ethel_10_11_24_all_1&n=2)
Robert F. Kennedy Jr.
My mom, Ethel Skakel Kennedy, passed peacefully into Heaven this morning. She was 96. She died in Boston surrounded by many of her nine surviving children and her friends. God gave her 34 grandchildren, 24 great-grandchildren, and the energy to give them all the attention they required. He blessed her with a rich and eventful life. Even as she declined in recent months, she never lost her sense of fun, her humor, her spark, her spunk, and her joie de vivre. She wrung joy from every moment, but for 56 years she has spoken with yearning of the day she would reunite with her beloved husband. She is with him now, with my brothers David and Michael, with her parents, her six siblings, all of whom predeceased her, and her “adopted” Kennedy siblings Jack, Kick, Joe, Teddy, Eunice, Jean, Rosemary, and Patricia. From the day she met my father, her new family observed that she was “more Kennedy than the Kennedys.” She was never more enthusiastic about the afterlife than when she considered that she would also be reunited with her many dogs, including 16 Irish setters — all conveniently named “Rusty.”
The cognitive dissonance that allowed her to keep two inconsistent truths in her heart at the same time without budging made my mother a collection of irreconcilable convictions. Among these was her ironic combination of deep — nearly blind — reverence for the Catholic Church and irreverence toward its clerics. She was at once starstruck by America’s presidents, all of whom she came to know personally, and at the same time skeptical of government and toward all figures of authority. She balanced her contempt for pretension and hypocrisy with a boundless tolerance for error and mistakes in others.
God also endowed her with a perpetual attitude of gratitude that fueled her taste for adventure and an irrepressible buoyancy in a life beset by a continuous parade of heartbreaking tragedies. Her sunny optimism eventually brought my shattered father back to life following the assassination of his brother and then helped her children to thrive after her husband’s assassination five years later.
Among her most defining qualities were moral and physical fearlessness. She was a peerless equestrian and held the high jump record on horseback, jumping 7′9′′ on a Quarter Horse. Critics named her among the best female amateur tennis players, and she was a competitive diver. But she did every sport well — from football to skiing, waterskiing and kayaking. Her disciplined stoicism and her deep faith in God enabled her to endure over ten years of pregnancy without complaint. She also suffered the murders of her husband and Uncle Jack, and the early deaths of two of her children. Various air crashes killed both of her parents, her brother, her sister-in-law, and her nephew John. She never enjoyed flying, but her worry never stopped her from boarding a plane. While giving short shrift to her own monumental suffering, she always showed intense compassion for others.
My mother invented tough love, and she could be hard on her children when we didn’t live up to her expectations. But she was also intensely loyal, and we always knew that she would stand fiercely behind us when we came under attack by others. She was our role model for self-discipline, for resilience, and for self-confidence. She deeded to each of her 11 children her love of good stories, her athleticism, her competitive spirit, and the deep curiosity about the world, and the intense interest in people of all backgrounds, which caused her to pepper everyone she met — from cab drivers to presidents — with a relentless cascade of questions about their lives. She also gave us all her love of language and for good storytelling. I credit her for all my virtues. I’m grateful for her generosity in overlooking my faults.

God also endowed her with a perpetual attitude of gratitude that fueled her taste for adventure and an irrepressible buoyancy in a life beset by a continuous parade of heartbreaking tragedies. Her sunny optimism eventually brought my shattered father back to life following the assassination of his brother and then helped her children to thrive after her husband’s assassination five years later. Among her most defining qualities were moral and physical fearlessness. She was a peerless equestrian and held the high jump record on horseback, jumping 7′9′′ on a Quarter Horse. Critics named her among the best female amateur tennis players, and she was a competitive diver. But she did every sport well — from football to skiing, waterskiing and kayaking. Her disciplined stoicism and her deep faith in God enabled her to endure over ten years of pregnancy without complaint. She also suffered the murders of her husband and Uncle Jack, and the early deaths of two of her children. Various air crashes killed both of her parents, her brother, her sister-in-law, and her nephew John. She never enjoyed flying, but her worry never stopped her from boarding a plane. While giving short shrift to her own monumental suffering, she always showed intense compassion for others. My mother invented tough love, and she could be hard on her children when we didn’t live up to her expectations. But she was also intensely loyal, and we always knew that she would stand fiercely behind us when we came under attack by others. She was our role model for self-discipline, for resilience, and for self-confidence. She deeded to each of her 11 children her love of good stories, her athleticism, her competitive spirit, and the deep curiosity about the world, and the intense interest in people of all backgrounds, which caused her to pepper everyone she met — from cab drivers to presidents — with a relentless cascade of questions about their lives. She also gave us all her love of language and for good storytelling. I credit her for all my virtues. I’m grateful for her generosity in overlooking my faults. | | ©2024 • • • • PAID FOR BY TEAM KENNEDY | | PAID FOR BY TEAM KENNEDY P.O. industry donations into political campaigns ahead of this November’s
election.

As Slate says, “Faceless, but more menacing and powerful than ever, with
four times the money, crypto is wreaking havoc on the 2024 election
cycle.” The crypto industry’s super PAC Fairshake has dropped $203 million

corporate spending.

fill Congress with right-wing politicians who will vote in their best

running tens of millions of dollars worth of ads in critical Senate and
House districts without even mentioning the issue of cryptocurrency.

| **ABOUT NELLA**
**New Mexico is Nella Domenici’s home. She was born in Albuquerque and lived for most of her childhood in a home near the intersection of Lomas and Monroe with her seven siblings, and her parents - Pete and Nancy Domenici. Nella began her education at Our Lady of Fatima, where she learned the values she holds today. Nella is a proud third-generation New Mexican, devoted mother of two, step-mom of four, and the wife of a Navy Veteran. Nella’s family’s roots run deep in New Mexico and she and her husband Pat enjoy their family home in New Mexico that they have owned for nearly twenty years.

Like most New Mexicans, Nella Domenici understands the importance of hard work. She waited tables to help pay for her undergraduate degree from Georgetown University, and worked her way through night school at Georgetown Law while holding down a full time job. She then graduated from Harvard Business School as a Baker Scholar, top 5% of the class, while 9 months pregnant.

Nella began her career at the bottom and worked her way up through the complex finance world, eventually serving as CFO for one of the world’s largest, most successful investment firms. In her career, Nella advised, invested in, grew, and led many companies, and served on public company boards. The industries she has worked in are vast and include areas such as health care, AI, food service, lodging, commercial real estate, mortgage lending, and consumer products. These companies have ranged from small family-owned businesses, to rapidly growing venture backed enterprises, to a Fortune 200 company. Several of these have been headquartered in New Mexico. Collectively, the companies Nella has been heavily involved with have employed thousands of Americans.

Like her father and mother, Nella has been a warrior for those who most need an advocate: for women competing in academics or business, for families dealing with mental illness, and for those without access to quality healthcare or education. **

clean_body: Our window of opportunity in this race is rapidly closing, and this is a real chance to flip a “safe blue” seat, embarrass the Democrats, and secure a fool-proof Senate GOP Majority. | Peter, Last month, I wrote to tell you about something exciting happening down in New Mexico. Since then, I’ve traveled to the Land of Enchantment to campaign in person with Republican Nella Domenici , who is closing in on Martin Heinrich in the U.S. Senate race. Nella has been fighting tooth and nail, and it’s been paying off. Heinrich is polling under 50% and a double-digit percentage of voters are still undecided – even as early and mail-in voting has begun. – something the Democrats NEVER saw coming. Nella has a top-notch team and passionate volunteers working around the clock. Our window of opportunity in this race is rapidly closing , and this is a real chance to flip a “safe blue” seat, embarrass the Democrats, and secure a fool-proof Senate GOP Majority. Senator Cynthia Lummis | ABOUT NELLA New Mexico is Nella Domenici’s home. She was born in Albuquerque and lived for most of her childhood in a home near the intersection of Lomas and Monroe with her seven siblings, and her parents - Pete and Nancy Domenici. Nella began her education at Our Lady of Fatima, where she learned the values she holds today. Nella is a proud third-generation New Mexican, devoted mother of two, step-mom of four, and the wife of a Navy Veteran. Nella’s family’s roots run deep in New Mexico and she and her husband Pat enjoy their family home in New Mexico that they have owned for nearly twenty years. Like most New Mexicans, Nella Domenici understands the importance of hard work. She waited tables to help pay for her undergraduate degree from Georgetown University, and worked her way through night school at Georgetown Law while holding down a full time job. She then graduated from Harvard Business School as a Baker Scholar, top 5% of the class, while 9 months pregnant. Nella began her career at the bottom and worked her way up through the complex finance world, eventually serving as CFO for one of the world’s largest, most successful investment firms. In her career, Nella advised, invested in, grew, and led many companies, and served on public company boards. The industries she has worked in are vast and include areas such as health care, AI, food service, lodging, commercial real estate, mortgage lending, and consumer products. These companies have ranged from small family-owned businesses, to rapidly growing venture backed enterprises, to a Fortune 200 company. Several of these have been headquartered in New Mexico. Collectively, the companies Nella has been heavily involved with have employed thousands of Americans. Like her father and mother, Nella has been a warrior for those who most need an advocate: for women competing in academics or business, for families dealing with mental illness, and for those without access to quality healthcare or education. subject: I didn’t run for the sake of making history
